title: Scenario Match
help: One scenario = one question in Scenario Match, one example scenario in the Feature Book and one 'when to use it' puzzle in Packs, Free Play, Speed Round and the Daily Challenge. 'need' is the first-person ask the player reads (it must not name the feature). 'text' is how Copilot helps, shown after the answer and in the Feature Book. 'options' lists three other feature ids that look plausible but are not the best fit; use { "feature": id, "why": text } to say why one is not. Run tools\build.ps1 to check this file; it prints friendly errors and refreshes data\scenarios.js.

scenarios.title: Multilingual project call
scenarios.need: My weekly project meeting has an engineer in Tokyo and a manager in Brazil, and I want everyone to speak and hear the discussion in their own language as it happens.
scenarios.text: A Japanese engineer and a Brazilian project manager each speak and listen in their own language during the weekly project meeting.

scenarios.title: Supplier negotiation
scenarios.need: I'm on a one-to-one Teams call with a supplier in Munich who's more comfortable in German, and I want us each to hear the other in our own language, live.
scenarios.text: A procurement lead in Sydney talks with a German supplier in a one-to-one Teams call, each hearing the other interpreted.

scenarios.title: Regional clinic huddle
scenarios.need: Our regional health team is half Spanish and half English speakers, and I want each person to listen in their preferred language while the meeting is happening.
scenarios.text: A health network's regional team mixes Spanish and English speakers in one meeting, with each person listening in their preferred language.

scenarios.title: Find a partner agent
scenarios.need: I want to browse and add a ready-made agent from a Microsoft partner that works with our team's planning tool, without building anything myself.
scenarios.text: A project lead browses the store and adds a partner-built agent that works with their team's planning tool.

scenarios.title: Approve a team's agent
scenarios.need: I'm the admin, and a colleague has submitted an agent they built in Copilot Studio. I want to approve it so staff can discover and add it where they browse other agents.
scenarios.text: An admin reviews an agent a maker submitted from Copilot Studio and publishes it so colleagues can find it.

scenarios.title: Share company know-how
scenarios.need: I'm a new starter and want to find the HR policy agent our organisation built, among other agents I can add, without asking around for a link.
scenarios.text: An HR team's policy agent appears in the Built by your org collection, so new starters can find it themselves.

scenarios.title: Policy Q&A agent
scenarios.need: I'm in HR and want to make my own helper, answering only from our leave policy, by describing it in plain words in Copilot, testing it, then sharing it with staff.
scenarios.text: HR builds an agent grounded in the leave policy so staff can ask questions instead of emailing the team.

scenarios.title: Project digest
scenarios.need: I want to describe and set up my own helper in Copilot that answers status questions from our team's SharePoint site and Teams chats, then share it so people stop pinging me.
scenarios.text: A project lead builds an agent over the team's SharePoint site and Teams chats for quick status updates.

scenarios.title: Onboarding buddy
scenarios.need: I lead a small team and want to create, in a few minutes, a helper new starters can ask how-do-I questions, answering only from our onboarding handbook.
scenarios.text: A team leader creates an agent from the onboarding handbook so new starters can ask how-do-I questions.

scenarios.title: Customer service agent
scenarios.need: I want a chat assistant on our online shop's website that answers order questions and passes tricky cases to a real person, built without writing code.
scenarios.text: A retailer builds an agent that answers order questions on its website and hands tricky cases to a human.

scenarios.title: IT helpdesk agent
scenarios.need: Our IT team wants to build its own chat assistant in Teams that walks staff through password resets and logs a ticket when they get stuck.
scenarios.text: An IT team publishes an agent in Teams that guides staff through password resets and raises tickets.

scenarios.title: Expense approvals
scenarios.need: Our finance team wants to build an assistant so staff can submit expense claims and check approval status just by chatting, linked to our approval process.
scenarios.text: A finance team connects an agent to approval workflows so staff can submit and track expenses by chat.

scenarios.title: Agent performance review
scenarios.need: I built our staff help agent last month and now want to see how often it's used, how satisfied people are and where its answers fall short.
scenarios.text: An HR maker opens the agent's analytics to review usage, satisfaction scores and feedback comments, then improves the answers that left staff unhappy.

scenarios.title: Sales playbook coach
scenarios.need: I'm a developer. I want a sales assistant inside Copilot that answers from our playbook library, using Copilot's own AI rather than a model we host ourselves.
scenarios.text: A sales team publishes an agent that answers questions from its playbook and product sheets, grounded in a SharePoint library.

scenarios.title: Compliance checker
scenarios.need: I'm setting up an assistant in Copilot that answers policy questions only from our approved documents, with citations, without building or hosting any AI of our own.
scenarios.text: A risk team configures an agent that answers policy questions with citations from approved documents only.

scenarios.title: Engineering onboarding
scenarios.need: I'm a developer and want to ship an assistant in Copilot that knows our architecture docs and coding standards, described in a settings file rather than custom code.
scenarios.text: A software team ships an agent that knows its architecture docs and coding standards.

scenarios.title: Proprietary model
scenarios.need: Our law firm has built and hosts its own legal research model, and we want lawyers to use it from inside Copilot with our model doing the thinking.
scenarios.text: A law firm surfaces its own legal-research model inside Copilot as an agent, with its own model and logic doing the reasoning.

scenarios.title: Proactive reminders
scenarios.need: Our recruiting team wants an assistant in Teams, running on our own models and logic, that messages interviewers first to remind them to enter feedback.
scenarios.text: A recruiting team's agent nudges interviewers in Teams to enter their feedback.

scenarios.title: Foundry agent in Copilot
scenarios.need: Our engineers already built an agent in Microsoft Foundry with its own models, and we want staff to reach it from Copilot without rebuilding it.
scenarios.text: An engineering team publishes an existing Microsoft Foundry agent so staff can use it from Copilot.

scenarios.title: Wiki answers
scenarios.need: Our engineering wiki lives in Confluence, and I want everyone's Copilot to answer questions from it while respecting who can see which pages.
scenarios.text: A support team connects Confluence so Copilot can answer questions from the engineering wiki.

scenarios.title: Sales context
scenarios.need: Our account notes live in a third-party CRM, and I want Copilot to draw on them when I prepare for client meetings.
scenarios.text: A sales team connects its CRM so Copilot can draw on account notes when preparing for a meeting.

scenarios.title: File-share search
scenarios.need: We still keep old policies on a network drive in the office, and I want staff to be able to find them by asking Copilot.
scenarios.text: An IT team indexes a legacy network file share so staff can find old policies from Copilot.

scenarios.title: Invoice approval
scenarios.need: I want every submitted invoice to have its key fields pulled out, checked against our supplier records and sent for approval, exactly the same way every time.
scenarios.text: Finance extracts data from an invoice, validates it against records and routes it for approval.

scenarios.title: New-starter setup
scenarios.need: I want our onboarding agent to run a fixed, reliable set of steps whenever it hears someone new is starting: create their accounts, then tell their manager.
scenarios.text: HR triggers a flow that creates accounts and notifies the manager, called by an onboarding agent.

scenarios.title: Weekly report
scenarios.need: I want our latest figures compiled and a summary emailed to the operations team automatically every Monday, following the same steps each week.
scenarios.text: An operations team runs a flow each Monday to compile figures and email a summary.

scenarios.title: Legacy data entry
scenarios.need: Our old accounting program can't link to any other system, so I want an agent to type invoice details into its screens for us.
scenarios.text: Finance has an agent copy invoice details into an older system that has no integration.

scenarios.title: Portal checks
scenarios.need: I want an agent to sign in to a supplier's website and download the daily order status for us, because the site has no way to link to our systems.
scenarios.text: An operations agent logs into a supplier portal to download daily order status.

scenarios.title: Report grab
scenarios.need: I want an agent to open a desktop reporting app that has no integration options, export a report and save it to our SharePoint library.
scenarios.text: An analyst's agent opens a desktop app, exports a report and saves it to SharePoint.

scenarios.title: HR front door
scenarios.need: We already have separate agents for leave, payroll and benefits. I want one main HR agent that sends each question to the right one.
scenarios.text: A main HR agent routes questions to separate leave, payroll and benefits agents.

scenarios.title: Support triage
scenarios.need: Our service agent keeps getting technical questions, and the IT team already owns an agent for those. I want ours to hand them over automatically.
scenarios.text: A service agent hands technical issues to an IT agent owned by another team.

scenarios.title: Sales bundle
scenarios.need: Our deal-desk agent needs prices from the pricing team's agent and terms from the contracts team's agent to put together one proposal.
scenarios.text: A deal-desk agent calls pricing and contract agents to assemble a proposal.

scenarios.title: Law firm drafting
scenarios.need: I want first drafts of our contracts to come out in our firm's house style, by teaching a model from our best past contracts.
scenarios.text: A firm tunes an agent on its best contracts so first drafts reflect its house style.

scenarios.title: Expert Q&A
scenarios.need: Our senior engineers' know-how sits in years of project reports. I want a specialist model trained on them so staff get expert-level answers.
scenarios.text: An engineering company tunes an agent on past project reports so staff get expert-level answers.

scenarios.title: Consistent summaries
scenarios.need: I want every claims file summary to follow exactly the same structure and standards, using a model taught our own way of summarising.
scenarios.text: An insurer tunes summaries so every claims file follows the same structure.

scenarios.title: Ticketing tool
scenarios.need: Our platform team's ticketing system already offers its actions through an open standard for AI tools. I want our agent to look up and update tickets through it.
scenarios.text: A platform team lets an agent call its internal ticketing system through an MCP server.

scenarios.title: Data lookup
scenarios.need: Our data team has exposed the company's figures as a tool server using an open standard, and I want my agent to query it directly.
scenarios.text: An analyst's agent queries a company data service that is exposed through MCP.

scenarios.title: Reusable server
scenarios.need: We're a partner and want to publish our tools once, using an open standard, so lots of different makers' agents can plug into them.
scenarios.text: A partner publishes one MCP server that many makers' agents can reuse.

scenarios.title: Declarative agent
scenarios.need: I'm a developer and want to start a sales agent from a template in my code editor, then debug it locally before publishing.
scenarios.text: A developer scaffolds a declarative agent for the sales team and debugs it locally.

scenarios.title: Custom engine agent
scenarios.need: I've coded our support assistant and want one set of developer tools in my editor to debug it, test it and publish it to Teams.
scenarios.text: A software company builds a custom engine agent with the Agents SDK and publishes it to Teams.

scenarios.title: Internal Teams app
scenarios.need: I want to ship a simple tab app to our staff inside Teams, starting from a ready-made project template in my code editor.
scenarios.text: A company developer starts from a ready-made template in their code editor and ships a tab app to staff in Teams.

scenarios.title: Account briefing
scenarios.need: I want a cited briefing on our customer before Friday's renewal call, drawing on our recent emails, meeting notes and current public news.
scenarios.text: Before a renewal call, ask for a briefing on the customer using recent emails, meeting notes and public news, with cited sources.

scenarios.title: Market landscape scan
scenarios.need: I want a sectioned overview of our competitors and market trends before strategy day, drawn only from the web, with citations I can check.
scenarios.text: A strategy lead asks for a competitor and market-trend overview, scoped to the web only, and gets a sectioned report with citations to check.

scenarios.title: Policy comparison
scenarios.need: I want to know how our internal leave guidance stacks up against current public employment rules, and I'm happy to answer a few questions first to steer it.
scenarios.text: An HR manager asks how internal leave guidance compares with current public rules, answering clarifying questions to steer the investigation.

scenarios.title: Program handover history
scenarios.need: I'm inheriting a year-long program and want an organised, cited account of its key decisions, drawn from the emails, meetings, chats and files I can access.
scenarios.text: A new program lead asks for a structured report on the program's history and key decisions, drawn from work emails, meetings, chats and files, with citations to check.

scenarios.title: Expansion assessment
scenarios.need: I need a shareable report on whether to open an office in Auckland, weighing our internal strategy papers against public market data, with charts and sources.
scenarios.text: A strategy manager asks for an expansion assessment that combines internal strategy documents with web sources, and gets an organised report with visuals and citations.

scenarios.title: Top-seller review
scenarios.need: I have sales exports from six stores in separate files and want to know which products sell best and where the odd results are, without merging them first.
scenarios.text: A retail manager attaches several store sales exports and asks which products perform best and where outliers appear, without merging the files first.

scenarios.title: Survey trend check
scenarios.need: I've got our staff engagement survey results as a CSV and want trends by department, any surprising outliers and a chart for the leadership update.
scenarios.text: An HR partner uploads engagement survey results as a CSV and asks for trends by department and any surprising outliers, with a chart for the leadership update.

scenarios.title: Budget variance check
scenarios.need: I want to compare our budget and actuals workbooks to see where spending drifted most, and check the calculation steps myself before I report it.
scenarios.text: A finance lead attaches budget and actuals workbooks, asks where spending drifted most, and checks the Python on screen to confirm the numbers add up.

scenarios.title: Support ticket trends
scenarios.need: I have a CSV export of 12 months of support tickets and want to see which categories are growing, with a chart and working I can check.
scenarios.text: A service desk lead attaches a year of ticket exports, asks which categories are growing month on month, and gets a trend chart plus the Python it ran to get there.

scenarios.title: Unusual traffic days
scenarios.need: I've exported a year of daily website visits and want to find the days that look unusual and understand what sets them apart, step by step.
scenarios.text: A digital marketer attaches a website-traffic export and asks for unusual days; it reasons step by step, flags the outliers in a table and charts them against the normal trend.

scenarios.title: Keeping to the agenda
scenarios.need: Our project kick-offs always overrun. During the meeting I want agenda topics with timing reminders that keep everyone on schedule.
scenarios.text: A project manager gives the agent the agenda with time allocations, and its on-screen agenda timer and countdowns keep the kick-off from overrunning.

scenarios.title: Requirements workshop
scenarios.need: I want an AI participant in tomorrow's requirements workshop that can draft the business requirements document in Word during or straight after the session.
scenarios.text: In a requirements workshop, a consultant asks the agent to draft a business requirements document in Word during or straight after the meeting.

scenarios.title: Teams Room huddle
scenarios.need: Our leadership team meets in a Teams Room, and I want shared live notes everyone can edit, with timers keeping each agenda item moving.
scenarios.text: A school leadership team meets in a Teams Room; everyone edits the shared live notes while timers keep each agenda topic moving.

scenarios.title: Fortnightly status update
scenarios.need: I want a concise status report for the last two weeks, written from our project plan's task data, that I can share with stakeholders as a SharePoint newsletter.
scenarios.text: A project lead opens the Reports tab, picks the last two weeks and a concise length, and shares the result with stakeholders as a SharePoint newsletter.

scenarios.title: Delegate a first draft
scenarios.need: I want to assign a task in our project plan to AI, have it draft a launch announcement outline, then review the draft once it's ready.
scenarios.text: A marketing coordinator assigns the agent a task to draft a launch announcement outline, then reviews it once the task shows as ready for review.

scenarios.title: Goal to task list
scenarios.need: I've got a high-level goal, opening the new depot by June, and want it turned into tasks in our project plan that I can then refine.
scenarios.text: An operations manager on a premium plan types a high-level goal like 'open the new depot by June' and has the agent generate tasks to refine.

scenarios.title: New starter benefits
scenarios.need: I'm a new starter and want to ask which benefits I'm eligible for and how to enrol, right in Copilot, instead of emailing HR.
scenarios.text: A new starter asks which benefits they're eligible for and how to enrol, and gets an answer drawn from the organisation's HR knowledge instead of emailing HR.

scenarios.title: Device setup help
scenarios.need: My new work tablet won't let me sign in, and I want guided fix-it steps from our IT help in Copilot instead of hunting for the right portal.
scenarios.text: A clinic nurse asks how to set up a new tablet and fix a sign-in problem, getting guided steps from the IT agent.

scenarios.title: Sandbox-first rollout
scenarios.need: I'm deploying Microsoft's prebuilt HR and IT starter agents for a client and want to test the HR one in a sandbox and catch configuration issues first.
scenarios.text: A consultant deploys the HR starter in a sandbox, runs FlightCheck to catch configuration issues, then deploys the IT starter separately.

scenarios.title: Cleaning up ownerless agents
scenarios.need: I need to find the agents a lecturer shared with staff before her account was deleted, now that nobody looks after them, and block or remove them.
scenarios.text: After a staff member's account is deleted, a university IT admin uses the Agents without owners card to find their shared agents and block or delete them.

scenarios.title: Audit-ready agent list
scenarios.need: Our auditors want a spreadsheet of every agent available to staff, filtered to those from outside publishers, showing who owns each one.
scenarios.text: A public-sector compliance lead exports the registry to CSV, filtered by publisher type, and hands the list to auditors.

scenarios.title: Reviewing agent risk
scenarios.need: I want to open a finance agent's details in the Microsoft 365 admin center and see whether Purview, Entra or Defender rate it high, medium or low risk.
scenarios.text: With the right licence, a bank's security analyst opens an agent's Risk details to see high, medium and low signals from Microsoft Purview, Entra and Defender.

scenarios.title: Write the role charter
scenarios.need: I'm setting up a network of volunteer Copilot helpers in each department and want Microsoft's guidance for writing their role charter before I invite people.
scenarios.text: A public-sector adoption lead uses Microsoft's guide to building a Champion community to draft a one-page role charter, then invites a Champion from each department.

scenarios.title: Learn from peers
scenarios.need: I train hospital staff on Copilot and want to join community calls and ask people at other organisations how they got staff using it.
scenarios.text: A hospital digital trainer joins a Driving Adoption call, watches an on-demand recording and asks the forum how other organisations got staff using Copilot.

scenarios.title: Share early wins
scenarios.need: I want a storytelling guide and sample adoption plan, from a community of people doing my job, to share early Copilot wins with our branch staff.
scenarios.text: A bank's internal-comms specialist uses the storytelling guide and sample adoption plan to share early wins with branch staff.

scenarios.title: Friday status report
scenarios.need: I want a draft status report every Friday, built from our project's Teams channel conversations and files, that I can edit before sharing.
scenarios.text: A project manager asks the agent to draft a weekly status report from the channel's conversations and files, then reviews and edits it before sharing.

scenarios.title: Deadline check
scenarios.need: I want to ask a dedicated expert for our campaign's Teams channel which deadlines are coming up, drawing on the channel's messages and shared files.
scenarios.text: A marketing lead in a campaign channel asks which deadlines are coming up and gets an answer drawn from the channel's messages and shared files.

scenarios.title: Meeting actions to tasks
scenarios.need: I want to approve the AI summary of our channel meeting, then have tasks with reminders created in the channel for the agreed actions.
scenarios.text: After a channel meeting, a programme officer approves the agent's summary, then asks it to create tasks with reminders for the agreed actions.

scenarios.title: Tailored company academy
scenarios.need: I lead learning and development and want to copy Microsoft's ready-made Copilot learning paths in our learning platform, swap in our own and publish it to sales.
scenarios.text: A manufacturer's L&D lead duplicates the academy, swaps in company-specific learning paths and publishes it to the sales and operations groups.

scenarios.title: Match training to licences
scenarios.need: I'm our Knowledge admin and want Microsoft's curated Copilot courses available only to staff who actually have a Copilot licence.
scenarios.text: A university's Knowledge admin restricts the academy to Copilot-licensed staff, so learning matches who actually has Copilot.

scenarios.title: Monthly Teams nudge
scenarios.need: I have Copilot and want a structured learning path from Microsoft I can dip into each month, to pick up one new skill before my customer calls.
scenarios.text: A sales rep with a Copilot licence opens the monthly Teams notification, picks a learning path and tries one new Copilot skill before their next customer call.

scenarios.title: Prep for a client call
scenarios.need: I've got a call with a client in an hour and want a quick rundown of our recent emails and meetings with them, plus some talking points.
scenarios.text: Ask for a summary of recent emails and meetings with a client, pointing to the account file with a slash, then draft talking points.

scenarios.title: Explain a policy
scenarios.need: I need our long HR leave policy explained in plain English, with the three things managers most need to know.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot to summarise a long HR policy document in plain English and list the three things managers most need to know.

scenarios.title: Draft a stakeholder update
scenarios.need: I want a plain-English status update based on this week's team meeting, then to adjust its tone and length with a couple of follow-up requests.
scenarios.text: A project officer asks for a plain-English status update from this week's team meeting, then refines the tone and length with follow-up requests.

scenarios.title: Web and work files together
scenarios.need: I want to search the web and multiple internal documents at the same time.
scenarios.text: Copilot Chat can draw on the web and, through Work IQ, the work files you can access, so one question gets a single combined answer instead of two separate searches.

scenarios.title: Name ideas for a programme
scenarios.need: I need ten catchy name ideas for our new staff wellbeing programme, then want to narrow the shortlist in a quick back-and-forth.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot Chat for name ideas with a line on each, then narrow the shortlist with follow-up requests such as 'make them shorter' or 'more playful'.

scenarios.title: Explain a finance term
scenarios.need: I've got a finance meeting soon and want a quick, plain-English explanation of what EBITDA means, with a simple example I can follow.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot Chat for a plain-English explanation with a simple example. It can use the web to ground the answer, and you can keep asking follow-ups until it makes sense.

scenarios.title: Catch up after time away
scenarios.need: I've been off sick for three days and want one catch-up on what I missed across my email, Teams chats and meetings.
scenarios.text: Copilot Chat can draw on your emails, chats and meetings through Work IQ to summarise what happened while you were away and what still needs your attention.

scenarios.title: Pre-rollout oversharing check
scenarios.need: We're about to switch Copilot on, and I want Microsoft's step-by-step oversharing plan that sits inside its wider framework for securing, managing and measuring Copilot.
scenarios.text: A council's IT team works through the oversharing blueprint in the security and governance pillar before switching Copilot on for staff.

scenarios.title: Agent and web-search rules
scenarios.need: I'm setting rules for how staff build and use agents and whether Copilot can search the web, and I want Microsoft's management guidance from its overall Copilot governance framework.
scenarios.text: Using the management pillar's admin center scenarios, a retail IT admin decides how staff create and use agents and whether Copilot can search the web.

scenarios.title: Proving adoption and value
scenarios.need: I want the measurement part of Microsoft's end-to-end Copilot governance framework, with its playbooks, so I can prove adoption and value to our executives.
scenarios.text: A change lead at a bank uses the measurement pillar's Copilot Dashboard and analytics playbooks to show executives how Copilot is being adopted.

scenarios.title: On-brand event banner
scenarios.need: I need a wide banner image for our customer webinar that sticks to our organisation's official colours, logo and style.
scenarios.text: A marketing coordinator describes a webinar banner and, if the organisation provides an official Brand Kit, gets a draft that stays on brand.

scenarios.title: Classroom infographic
scenarios.need: I want an eye-catching visual explaining the water cycle for my Year 5 class, which I can refine and keep for later lessons.
scenarios.text: A teacher describes an infographic explaining the water cycle for Year 5, then refines it and saves it to their Library.

scenarios.title: Quick staff survey
scenarios.need: I want to describe a short staff pulse survey in the part of the Copilot app where I make posters and banners, and get a draft back to tweak.
scenarios.text: An HR officer describes a short staff pulse survey and gets a draft form to review and tweak before sharing it.

scenarios.title: Pre-rollout readiness check
scenarios.need: I want a page of recommended steps before our rollout, like enabling Copilot Chat and activating agents, so I can decide what to tackle first.
scenarios.text: Before a rollout, a university IT lead checks the Readiness page's recommended steps, like enabling Copilot Chat and activating agents, to decide what to tackle first.

scenarios.title: Team adoption check-in
scenarios.need: I'm a sales manager with no admin rights, and I want to see how often my own team uses Copilot so I know where some coaching could help.
scenarios.text: A sales manager reviews her group's adoption metrics to see how often the team uses Copilot and where coaching might help.

scenarios.title: Telling the impact story
scenarios.need: I want to show our executives what impact Copilot is having on work and how staff feel about it, with survey results alongside the usage numbers.
scenarios.text: A change manager at a health provider combines impact metrics with survey-based sentiment to tell executives how Copilot is landing with staff.

scenarios.title: Benchmarking against peers
scenarios.need: Our COO wants to know whether our share of active Copilot users is ahead of or behind similar companies, and similar groups inside our own business.
scenarios.text: An insights analyst opens the percentage of active Copilot users metric, selects Show benchmark, and compares the trend with an internal cohort of similar employees and with similar companies.

scenarios.title: Compare supplier pages
scenarios.need: I have three supplier websites open in my browser and want their prices, delivery terms and warranties compared side by side, without copying anything.
scenarios.text: A buyer opens three supplier pages and asks Copilot to compare prices, delivery terms and warranty details across the tabs.

scenarios.title: Skim before you read
scenarios.need: I've just opened a very long report on a website and want a quick summary beside it before deciding whether to read the whole thing.
scenarios.text: A policy analyst opens a long report on the web and asks Copilot to summarise it before deciding whether to read the full text.

scenarios.title: Supervised browsing
scenarios.need: I want Copilot to work through the travel booking sites open in my browser while I watch, and stop to check with me before it books anything.
scenarios.text: Where Browse with Copilot is available, a travel coordinator watches it work through open tabs and takes over when it asks for attention before booking.

scenarios.title: Webinar video recap
scenarios.need: I'm watching an hour-long product webinar on a vendor's website and want the key points pulled out beside the video, so I don't have to sit through it all.
scenarios.text: A new starter watching a long product webinar online asks Copilot in the Edge side pane to summarise the video, which works when the video has a transcript or captions.

scenarios.title: Questions about a web page
scenarios.need: I'm reading a long government guidance page in my browser and want to ask which rules apply to our casual staff, right beside the page.
scenarios.text: A payroll officer signed in with a work account asks Copilot in the Edge side pane which parts of a government guidance page apply to casual staff, with enterprise data protection applied.

scenarios.title: Pulse survey check
scenarios.need: I'm sending an employee pulse survey and want the questions drafted for me, then checked for leading or double-barrelled wording.
scenarios.text: An HR partner describes an employee pulse survey, lets Copilot draft the questions, then asks it to review them for leading or double-barrelled wording before sending.

scenarios.title: Class quiz in minutes
scenarios.need: I want a quick multiple-choice quiz on this week's fractions topic that my students can answer online, ready for me to tweak.
scenarios.text: A teacher describes this week's topic and Copilot drafts a quiz with questions and answer options, ready to keep, refine or regenerate.

scenarios.title: Resident feedback survey
scenarios.need: I need a resident feedback questionnaire I can share by QR code, then a summary of what people said once the responses come in.
scenarios.text: A council officer drafts a resident feedback form with Copilot, shares it by QR code, then asks Copilot to summarise the responses into key findings.

scenarios.title: Event registration form
scenarios.need: I need a sign-up questionnaire for our end-of-year staff event that asks about dietary needs and which session people want to attend.
scenarios.text: Describe the event and Copilot drafts a title, questions and answer options, such as dietary needs and session choices, for you to review before sharing.

scenarios.title: Recap page changes
scenarios.need: I've made lots of edits to our shared campaign planning page this week and want them summarised in one update my colleagues can read.
scenarios.text: A marketing lead asks Copilot to capture and summarise the updates they made to the campaign planning page in the Recap pane, where colleagues can read them.

scenarios.title: Meeting notes with tasks
scenarios.need: I want shared notes written during our weekly stand-up as we talk, with suggested tasks turned into components the whole team can edit.
scenarios.text: An operations manager lets Copilot generate collaborative notes during the weekly stand-up, then shares the suggested tasks as components the whole team can edit.

scenarios.title: Web answer onto the page
scenarios.need: I want to ask a web question about exam-preparation techniques and drop the answer straight onto our shared staff planning workspace.
scenarios.text: A school coordinator asks the Copilot chat a web question on exam-preparation techniques and inserts the answer onto the staff planning page.

scenarios.title: Work answer for the team
scenarios.need: I want to ask about the decisions in last month's project emails and insert the answer into our team's shared workspace for everyone to edit.
scenarios.text: Copilot's chat in Loop answers work questions as well as web ones, and you can insert the answer onto the page, where colleagues can read it and keep building on it.

scenarios.title: Compare supplier proposals
scenarios.need: I've got two supplier proposals saved in my personal files and want the key differences in price and delivery, without opening both.
scenarios.text: A procurement officer selects two supplier proposals and asks Copilot to compare them and list the key differences in price terms and delivery commitments.

scenarios.title: Listen to a board paper
scenarios.need: I want to listen to the key points of a long board paper stored in my files while I walk to the meeting.
scenarios.text: A finance manager turns a long board paper into an audio overview and listens to the key points on the way to a meeting.

scenarios.title: Ask across inspection reports
scenarios.need: I want to ask one question across five site inspection reports in my files to find which sites still have open safety actions.
scenarios.text: A site manager asks one question across several inspection reports, without opening each file, to find which sites still have open safety actions.

scenarios.title: Gist of a file before opening
scenarios.need: I want a short summary of a 50-page research PDF sitting in my files, straight from the file list, before deciding whether to read it.
scenarios.text: Copilot in OneDrive on the web can summarise a file you select, so you get the key points before deciding whether to open and read all of it.

scenarios.title: Section summary
scenarios.need: I want a whole section of my weekly check-in notes boiled down to key decisions and open questions before the steering meeting.
scenarios.text: A project manager asks Copilot to summarise a whole section of weekly check-in notes into key decisions and open questions before the steering meeting.

scenarios.title: Lesson outline
scenarios.need: My lesson ideas are scattered through my class notes, and I want them analysed and shaped into an outline for the first class of term.
scenarios.text: A teacher highlights scattered lesson ideas and asks Copilot to analyse them, then draft a presentation outline for the term's first class.

scenarios.title: Event plan brainstorm
scenarios.need: I've jotted venue and catering ideas in my notes and want an event plan drafted from them, plus a to-do list of what to book next.
scenarios.text: An events coordinator jots venue and catering ideas, then asks Copilot to brainstorm an event plan and a task list of what to book next.

scenarios.title: Agenda from rough notes
scenarios.need: I've got a page of rough ideas for next month's team offsite in my notes and want a meeting agenda drafted from them.
scenarios.text: Point Copilot at your ideas page and ask it to draft a meeting agenda, then have it pull any follow-ups into a task list.

scenarios.title: Flag the boss's emails
scenarios.need: I want every unread email from my manager flagged before stand-up, so I answer those requests first.
scenarios.text: A regional sales lead asks Copilot to flag all unread emails from their manager before a stand-up, so the boss's requests get answered first.

scenarios.title: Automatic reply for leave
scenarios.need: I'm on leave next Friday and want an out-of-office reply set for that day, without digging through settings menus.
scenarios.text: A school administrator taking leave next Friday asks Copilot to set an automatic reply for that day, without digging through settings menus.

scenarios.title: Plan tomorrow's calendar
scenarios.need: I want to know what's on my calendar tomorrow and get a note drafted asking to move a meeting that clashes.
scenarios.text: Before a busy day, a finance controller asks Copilot what's on their calendar tomorrow, then has it draft a note asking to reschedule a clash.

scenarios.title: Draft a new email
scenarios.need: I need to tell my team we've picked the new cleaning supplier and must sign by Friday, and want a draft message I can make shorter or longer.
scenarios.text: Start a new message and choose Draft (Draft with Copilot in classic Outlook). Copilot writes the email, and you can make it shorter, longer or change the tone before you keep it.

scenarios.title: Meeting invite from a thread
scenarios.need: I want a long email conversation with five suppliers turned into a meeting invitation, with a title, an agenda and everyone on it invited.
scenarios.text: In new Outlook, Schedule with Copilot turns an email into a meeting invitation, filling in the title and agenda, attaching the thread and inviting everyone on it.

scenarios.title: Catch up on a busy inbox
scenarios.need: I'm back from a conference and want to ask what my director emailed me about this week, then get a reply started for the most urgent one.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot in Outlook about your messages, such as what your director sent this week, then have it draft a reply you can review and edit before sending.

scenarios.title: Catch up on a project
scenarios.need: I'm back from leave and want to know what has changed across our project site's pages, lists and document libraries.
scenarios.text: A programme manager back from leave asks Copilot to catch them up on the project site's pages, lists and libraries.

scenarios.title: Build a tracking list
scenarios.need: I want a list set up on our team site to track the new-starter checklist, just by describing the columns and steps in plain English.
scenarios.text: An HR coordinator describes a new-starter checklist in plain English and asks Copilot to create a list to track it.

scenarios.title: Ask the site's agent
scenarios.need: I want to ask our policy site where the leave procedure lives, instead of searching through each document library myself.
scenarios.text: A council employee asks the policy site's agent where the leave procedure lives, rather than searching library by library.

scenarios.title: New site from a description
scenarios.need: I want a new intranet site for our graduate programme, with a welcome page, set up just by describing what it needs.
scenarios.text: Describe what you need in plain English and Copilot can create the site, along with pages, lists and libraries, for you to review and refine.

scenarios.title: Onboarding video Q&A
scenarios.need: I'm watching a recorded onboarding session and want to jump straight to the part where they explain the leave policy.
scenarios.text: A new starter opens a recorded onboarding session, asks Copilot where leave policy was covered and jumps straight to that timestamp.

scenarios.title: Town hall catch-up
scenarios.need: I missed the quarterly town hall and, while playing the recording, want the gist plus the exact moment the budget was announced.
scenarios.text: An executive who missed the quarterly town hall asks Copilot to summarise the recording, then checks the timestamp for the budget announcement.

scenarios.title: Training refresher
scenarios.need: I want to know what our recorded safety training said about incident reporting, so I can rewatch just that section.
scenarios.text: A nurse manager asks Copilot what a recorded safety training said about incident reporting, using the timestamp to rewatch just that section.

scenarios.title: What did I miss?
scenarios.need: I'm back from two weeks' leave and want to know what happened in my team's group chat, with a way to check the original messages.
scenarios.text: A ward manager back from two weeks off asks Copilot in the team's group chat what she missed, then clicks a source to check the rota change.

scenarios.title: Summarise a channel thread
scenarios.need: Our team's channel has a 90-reply campaign-launch thread, and I want its decisions and action items before the review without reading every reply.
scenarios.text: A marketing lead opens Copilot on a long campaign-launch thread in a channel and sees the decisions and action items before the review.

scenarios.title: Scope to last month
scenarios.need: I want to know what we agreed in our team's group chat last month about delivery dates, ignoring everything said since.
scenarios.text: A council project officer asks in the team's group chat, 'What did we agree last month about delivery dates?', so Copilot reads just that time frame.

scenarios.title: Gather shared links
scenarios.need: Our project group chat is full of links people posted over the past month, and I want a list of them without scrolling back through everything.
scenarios.text: A project coordinator opens Copilot in the team's group chat, asks 'What links were shared?', and gets a list with sources that jump back to each message.

scenarios.title: What one colleague said
scenarios.need: Our supplier contact Mei has posted a lot in a busy group chat about the delivery change, and I just want her points pulled together.
scenarios.text: A logistics coordinator asks Copilot in the group chat 'What did Mei say?' and gets her points summarised, with sources linking back to the original messages.

scenarios.title: Late-join catch-up
scenarios.need: I've joined our project meeting ten minutes late and want to quietly get up to speed without asking anyone to repeat themselves.
scenarios.text: An operations manager joins a project meeting ten minutes late, accepts Copilot's offer to catch up, and joins the discussion without asking anyone to repeat themselves.

scenarios.title: Find the disagreements
scenarios.need: I'm in a heated roadmap meeting and want to privately see where people disagree, plus questions I could ask to move things forward.
scenarios.text: A product manager in a heated roadmap discussion privately asks Copilot where the team disagrees and what questions could move things forward, then steers the group.

scenarios.title: Ideas into Word
scenarios.need: I want the ideas and feedback from our staff meeting, both spoken and typed in the meeting chat, listed in one long answer that I can take into Word.
scenarios.text: A school principal asks Copilot in the meeting chat to list the ideas and feedback from the transcript and chat, then exports the long answer to Word.

scenarios.title: Check a colleague's response
scenarios.need: I'm in a supplier review meeting and want to quietly check how our finance director responded to the pricing proposal earlier, without interrupting.
scenarios.text: During the meeting, a procurement lead privately asks Copilot how the finance director responded to the proposal and gets a summary of her points from the discussion so far.

scenarios.title: Pros and cons table mid-meeting
scenarios.need: I'm halfway through our options workshop and want every idea raised so far set out in a table with its pros and cons that I can open in Excel.
scenarios.text: Partway through a workshop, a project lead asks Copilot to create a table of the ideas discussed with their pros and cons, then exports it to Excel to keep working.

scenarios.title: Actions before wrap-up
scenarios.need: Our planning meeting has five minutes left, and I want the action items so far so I can confirm who owns each one before everyone drops off.
scenarios.text: With five minutes to go, a team leader asks Copilot in the meeting to list the action items so far, then reads them out so owners can confirm before the call ends.

scenarios.title: Smooth call transfers
scenarios.need: I'm transferring a transcribed customer call to a specialist and want them briefed, so the customer doesn't have to explain the whole problem again.
scenarios.text: Transfer a transcribed customer call to a specialist and Copilot drafts the transfer notes, so the customer isn't asked to repeat the whole problem.

scenarios.title: Candidate screening call
scenarios.need: I'm on a phone screening call with a candidate and want suggested follow-up questions and a list of action items before they hang up.
scenarios.text: A recruiter selects Copilot mid-call to get suggested follow-up questions and a list of action items before the candidate hangs up.

scenarios.title: Find the unresolved questions
scenarios.need: I've just finished a long phone call with a resident and want to ask which questions were asked, answered and left open, so I can plan the callback without replaying it.
scenarios.text: A council service officer opens a call recap and asks 'What questions were asked, answered, and unresolved?' to plan the callback without replaying the whole call.

scenarios.title: Retro theme sorting
scenarios.need: Our shared board is covered in sticky notes after the sprint retro, and I want them grouped into themes with headings so we can vote.
scenarios.text: After a sprint retro, the team adds sticky notes and Copilot groups them into coloured clusters with headings, so everyone can vote on the themes.

scenarios.title: Class brainstorm kick-start
scenarios.need: My class's brainstorm has stalled, and I want fresh idea suggestions to add as sticky notes on the board we're all using.
scenarios.text: A teacher enters a prompt, inserts the best suggested ideas as sticky notes and uses Generate more when the class needs fresh angles.

scenarios.title: Campaign workshop recap
scenarios.need: I want the sticky notes from our campaign brainstorm written up as an editable summary I can share with the wider team.
scenarios.text: A marketing manager summarises a campaign brainstorm's sticky notes into an editable Loop component and shares it with the wider team.

scenarios.title: More ideas for a risk session
scenarios.need: We're mapping project risks with sticky notes on a shared board, and I want extra ideas added for risks we haven't thought of yet.
scenarios.text: Enter a prompt in Suggest and Copilot offers ideas you can insert onto the board as sticky notes, then generate more when you need fresh angles.

scenarios.title: Standing writing preferences
scenarios.need: I'm tired of telling Copilot to lead with the headline number, use Australian spelling and keep it brief every single time I ask.
scenarios.text: A finance analyst writes custom instructions once: lead with the headline number, use Australian spelling, keep commentary brief. Copilot applies them to later answers.

scenarios.title: Context that sticks
scenarios.need: I keep re-explaining that I recruit for nursing roles, and I want Copilot to keep that in mind for future job-ad drafts.
scenarios.text: A hospital recruiter mentions the nursing roles they hire for; Copilot can save that detail so later job-ad drafts start with the right context.

scenarios.title: Temporary chat for tough topics
scenarios.need: I want to rehearse a tricky performance conversation with Copilot without it using or updating anything it has saved about me.
scenarios.text: A manager rehearses a difficult performance conversation in a temporary chat, so Copilot neither uses nor updates its saved memories.

scenarios.title: Hands-free on site
scenarios.need: I'm on a rooftop checking an air-conditioning unit with only my phone, and I want to show it to Copilot and talk it through hands free.
scenarios.text: A facilities technician on site shares their camera with Vision and talks to Copilot hands-free about the equipment in front of them.

scenarios.title: Capture client conversations
scenarios.need: I'm meeting a client face to face at a cafe and, with their permission, want my phone to capture the chat so I get a transcript and summary later.
scenarios.text: Where the app offers it, a consultant uses Record, with the client's permission, to capture an in-person meeting, then reads the transcript and summary afterwards.

scenarios.title: Voice chat between visits
scenarios.need: I'm walking from the car park to my next client visit and want to talk through my preparation with Copilot on my phone, hands free.
scenarios.text: A regional sales manager holds a hands-free voice conversation with Copilot to prepare for the next client visit while walking in from the car.

scenarios.title: Project knowledge hub
scenarios.need: I want our project plans, meeting notes and key emails gathered in one place, so I can ask about open risks and who owns each.
scenarios.text: A programme manager adds the project's plans, meeting notes and key emails as references, then asks for open risks and who owns each.

scenarios.title: Tender response prep
scenarios.need: I want the tender documents and our past proposals gathered together, then a list of requirements, gaps and first-draft answers based only on them.
scenarios.text: A bid writer adds the tender documents and past proposals, then asks Copilot to list requirements, spot gaps and draft first answers.

scenarios.title: Audio briefing
scenarios.need: I've gathered a set of new regulations in one place and want to listen to the key points before briefing my director.
scenarios.text: A policy officer adds the new regulations as references and plays the audio overview to grasp the key points before briefing her director.

scenarios.title: Themes across interviews
scenarios.need: I'll be collecting customer interview notes in one place over the next month and want to keep asking which themes keep coming up.
scenarios.text: Add each set of interview notes as references, then ask Copilot to find recurring themes, with answers based only on the sources you've gathered.

scenarios.title: Mind map of research
scenarios.need: I've pulled together a dozen articles and reports on hybrid work and want a visual map of how the main ideas connect.
scenarios.text: Gather the articles and reports as references, then ask Copilot for a mind map that shows how the main ideas and themes link together.

scenarios.title: Kick-off brief
scenarios.need: I've got a solid project brief from Copilot in chat, and now I want the team to refine the scope and owners with me in one shared, editable space.
scenarios.text: Pin Copilot's draft project brief to a Page, then invite the team to refine scope and owners together.

scenarios.title: Vendor comparison
scenarios.need: I want Copilot's comparison of our shortlisted suppliers kept as a table that procurement and finance can keep editing together.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot to compare shortlisted suppliers on cost, support and risk, then keep the table on a Page where procurement and finance can edit it together.

scenarios.title: Meeting follow-up
scenarios.need: I've got a meeting summary from Copilot in chat, and I want its action items moved somewhere the whole team can keep updating.
scenarios.text: A team lead turns action items from a meeting summary into a shared Page the whole team can update.

scenarios.title: Co-edit a run sheet
scenarios.need: I want to keep building on Copilot's answer about our conference run sheet, add a table, and co-edit it live with two colleagues.
scenarios.text: Open the answer in a Page beside chat, keep refining it with Copilot, add a table and share it so colleagues can co-edit in real time. Later you can convert it to Word or PDF.

scenarios.title: Reusable weekly update
scenarios.need: I retype the same request for a status update every Friday, and I want a tweaked version saved so I can reuse it.
scenarios.text: A project manager tweaks a Suggested prompt into a weekly status update and saves it to reuse every Friday.

scenarios.title: Share the winner
scenarios.need: My follow-up email request to Copilot works brilliantly, and I want the whole sales team in Teams to start from the same wording.
scenarios.text: A sales lead shares their best follow-up email prompt to the sales team in Teams, so everyone starts from the same proven wording.

scenarios.title: Starter prompts for new hires
scenarios.need: I'm an IT admin and want ready-made onboarding requests that our new-starter team can find and try right inside Copilot.
scenarios.text: An IT admin saves prompts for common onboarding questions and shares them to the new-starter team in Teams, so everyone in it can find them under Team prompts.

scenarios.title: Find that proposal
scenarios.need: I need the Contoso renewal email thread, the proposal file and the Teams chat about it, all in one list of results.
scenarios.text: A sales rep searches for 'Contoso renewal' and finds the email thread, the proposal file and the Teams chat in one results page.

scenarios.title: Decode company jargon
scenarios.need: I keep seeing an unfamiliar acronym in company emails and want a quick answer on what it means here, without asking around.
scenarios.text: A new starter searches for an unfamiliar acronym and can get an admin-curated answer, instead of asking around the team.

scenarios.title: Search beyond Microsoft 365
scenarios.need: I want to look once across our SharePoint files and the connected support knowledge base, then carry on drafting a customer reply.
scenarios.text: A support lead searches once across SharePoint files and a connected third-party knowledge base, then continues in Chat to draft a reply.

scenarios.title: Find a link in a chat
scenarios.need: I remember someone sharing the updated travel policy link in a Teams chat last month, but not who sent it or which chat it was in.
scenarios.text: One search in the Copilot app looks across chats as well as emails, files and meetings, so you can find the message even when you've forgotten who sent it.

scenarios.title: IT readiness planning
scenarios.need: I'm the IT lead preparing for Copilot and want Microsoft's downloadable technical readiness guide, plus guidance on deciding who gets licences first.
scenarios.text: An IT lead at a council works through the Technical Readiness Guide, then uses the licence allocation guide to decide who gets Copilot first.

scenarios.title: User enablement kick-off
scenarios.need: I want ready-to-send onboarding emails and Prompt-a-thon materials from Microsoft, so our store managers actually start trying Copilot.
scenarios.text: A retail learning manager sends the ready-to-send onboarding emails and runs a Prompt-a-thon from the engagement tools, so store managers start trying Copilot.

scenarios.title: Executive sponsor briefing
scenarios.need: Our chief operating officer wants a short Microsoft guide for leaders on what a Copilot rollout involves before agreeing to sponsor it.
scenarios.text: A hospital's chief operating officer reads the Implementation Summary Guide for Leaders to understand what a Copilot rollout involves before backing the programme.

scenarios.title: Licence value check
scenarios.need: I want to check in the Microsoft 365 admin center what share of our licensed hospital staff have actually tried Copilot over the past few weeks.
scenarios.text: A hospital IT admin checks the active users rate for licensed staff over recent weeks, then plans extra training if few people are trying Copilot.

scenarios.title: Launch momentum tracking
scenarios.need: We just ran a month-long awareness campaign, and I want to check in the admin center whether daily Copilot activity rose across Word, Teams and Outlook.
scenarios.text: A retailer's change manager runs a Copilot awareness month, then uses the trend view to see whether daily activity rises across apps.

scenarios.title: Chat-only rollout check
scenarios.need: I want to count, in the admin center, how many staff without a paid Copilot licence use the free chat, and get a tip for lifting that number.
scenarios.text: A council's digital team checks how many unlicensed staff use Copilot Chat, then follows the recommendation card's tip to pin Copilot in apps like Teams and Outlook.

scenarios.title: Confidential HR meeting
scenarios.need: I'm running a sensitive HR case meeting and want AI notes and tasks during it, but nothing transcribed or recorded.
scenarios.text: An HR partner sets the meeting to 'Only during the meeting', then starts Copilot for notes and tasks on a sensitive case without a transcript or recording.

scenarios.title: Contract strategy huddle
scenarios.need: We're holding an internal contract-strategy huddle, and I want AI to list our tasks live while making sure no transcript is created automatically.
scenarios.text: Finance leads choose 'Only during the meeting' for an internal contract-strategy huddle, so Copilot can list tasks live while nothing is transcribed automatically.

scenarios.title: Clinical incident review
scenarios.need: We're partway through a clinical incident review and I want AI to start capturing notes and tasks, but we can't have a transcript or recording running.
scenarios.text: A hospital quality team reviewing an incident starts Copilot partway through to capture notes and tasks, without a transcript or recording being started.

scenarios.title: HR policy assistant
scenarios.need: I'm a C# developer building one HR policy assistant on our chosen AI service, and I need it to run in Teams and on our intranet from the same code.
scenarios.text: An HR developer builds one policy-answering assistant on the company's chosen AI service and publishes it to Teams and the intranet website from the same code.

scenarios.title: Support bot across channels
scenarios.need: Our developers want to write one support assistant in code and serve it on our website, in Slack and in Teams, keeping track of each conversation.
scenarios.text: A retailer's developers build one support assistant and serve it on the website, in Slack and in Teams, using the SDK's state management to keep track of each conversation.

scenarios.title: Custom engine for Copilot
scenarios.need: Our hospital developers want to write a staff assistant in Python on our approved AI service, then make it available inside Microsoft 365 Copilot.
scenarios.text: A hospital IT team connects its approved AI service to an assistant for staff questions, then surfaces it inside Microsoft 365 Copilot as a custom engine agent.

scenarios.title: Grounded policy answers
scenarios.need: I'm building our own staff helper app and want it to fetch relevant SharePoint policy passages, limited to what each employee can already open.
scenarios.text: A public-sector developer grounds a staff helper in SharePoint policies via the Retrieval API, so answers only use content each employee may already access.

scenarios.title: Compliance review of interactions
scenarios.need: Our compliance team wants to pull staff's Copilot conversations into our own review software, so we can oversee how it's being used.
scenarios.text: A compliance team uses the Interaction Export API to bring Copilot interactions into its own review tooling for oversight.

scenarios.title: Usage dashboard for leadership
scenarios.need: I'm an IT admin and want Copilot adoption numbers fed automatically into the custom dashboard we built for our executive team.
scenarios.text: An IT admin pulls Copilot usage reports through Microsoft Graph into a custom dashboard, so executives can track how adoption is progressing.

scenarios.title: Quarantine unsanctioned agents
scenarios.need: I've found an AI agent nobody approved, and I want to quarantine it from one central place that governs all our agents, whatever platform they were built on.
scenarios.text: An IT admin reviews the registry, spots an AI agent nobody approved and quarantines it.

scenarios.title: Single source of truth
scenarios.need: Our risk team needs one trusted record of every AI agent we run, including ones built on open-source frameworks and other vendors' clouds, not just Microsoft's.
scenarios.text: A bank's risk team uses the registry as one source of truth for its AI agents, whether built on Microsoft platforms, open-source frameworks or partner clouds.

scenarios.title: Onboard a Studio-built agent
scenarios.need: I've just finished an agent in Copilot Studio and want IT to govern it in the same place as agents our developers built on other platforms.
scenarios.text: A maker finishes an agent in Copilot Studio and onboards it to Agent 365, so IT can govern it alongside agents built elsewhere.

scenarios.title: Blueprint once, govern many
scenarios.need: I want every new identity we create for our AI agents to inherit the same security policies from one reusable template, instead of setting each up by hand.
scenarios.text: An identity admin defines one blueprint so every agent identity created from it gets consistent security policies across the whole fleet.

scenarios.title: Sponsor leaves, ownership moves
scenarios.need: I want responsibility for each of our AI agents to pass to someone else automatically when the person accountable for it leaves the hospital, so none is left unowned.
scenarios.text: A hospital's governance lead relies on a Lifecycle Workflow to transfer sponsorship automatically when an agent's sponsor leaves, so no agent identity is left unowned.

scenarios.title: Bring a third-party agent
scenarios.need: Our developer built an agent in n8n and wants it to sign in with its own governed identity in our directory, just like our Microsoft-built agents.
scenarios.text: A developer connects an n8n agent to Microsoft Entra, so it gets its own governed agent identity and signs in just like the organisation's Microsoft-built agents.

scenarios.title: Sales prep without plumbing
scenarios.need: I'm building a custom agent for our sales team and want it to understand their mail, meetings, chats and files without us building a data pipeline.
scenarios.text: A sales team's custom agent pulls context from mail, meetings, chats and files through Work IQ, with no retrieval pipeline to build.

scenarios.title: Auditable internal assistant
scenarios.need: Our IT team is building an internal assistant that draws on workplace context, and we want every request checked by a policy engine and every tool call logged.
scenarios.text: An IT team builds an internal assistant on the Work IQ MCP server; a policy engine checks every request and every tool call is logged.

scenarios.title: Working storage for long tasks
scenarios.need: Our research agent runs long tasks over several days and needs proper working storage for its files, alongside an understanding of our workplace.
scenarios.text: A consultancy's research agent keeps its working files in a Work IQ workspace (SharePoint Embedded), giving a long-running task proper working storage.

scenarios.title: Pre-rollout oversharing sweep
scenarios.need: I want a list of SharePoint sites that have guests or the 'Everyone except external users' group in their permissions before our Copilot pilot starts.
scenarios.text: A council IT team runs the site permissions snapshot before a Copilot pilot to find sites with external guests or 'Everyone except external users' permissions.

scenarios.title: Check one person's reach
scenarios.need: I want to list every SharePoint site a departing contractor can get into, directly or through group membership, before their offboarding wraps up.
scenarios.text: A law firm's security analyst lists every site a departing contractor can reach, directly or through groups, before wrapping up their offboarding.

scenarios.title: Monthly sharing-links check
scenarios.need: I want to see each month which of our SharePoint sites created the most 'Anyone' sharing links over the past four weeks.
scenarios.text: A bank's compliance lead reviews the sharing links activity report each month to see which sites recently created the most Anyone links.

scenarios.title: Preventing exposure in Copilot
scenarios.need: I want a guided starting point in Purview that shows where our sensitive data sits, then walks me through one-click policies to stop it leaking into Copilot chats.
scenarios.text: A hospital security analyst picks the objective to prevent data exposure in Copilot interactions, then follows its guided workflow and one-click policies.

scenarios.title: Automating oversharing fixes
scenarios.need: I want a Purview workflow that spots where sensitive files are overshared and automatically fixes problems such as public sharing links.
scenarios.text: A university IT security lead uses the oversharing objective to spot risky sharing and automate fixes such as removing public sharing links.

scenarios.title: Watching agent behaviour
scenarios.need: I want views in our Purview data security tools that watch what our AI agents do with data and flag oversharing, data leaving the business or unusual access.
scenarios.text: A bank's risk team uses the AI observability dashboards to watch agent activity for oversharing, exfiltration and unusual access patterns.

scenarios.title: Order intake
scenarios.need: I want our agent to start on its own whenever an order record changes in our database, check the details and draft a customer confirmation.
scenarios.text: When an order record changes in Dataverse, the agent checks the details, drafts a customer confirmation and flags anything unusual for the fulfilment team.

scenarios.title: New starter setup
scenarios.need: I want our agent to get going by itself as soon as HR adds a new starter to our SharePoint list, then create onboarding tasks and draft a welcome email.
scenarios.text: When HR adds a new starter to a SharePoint list, the agent creates onboarding tasks in Planner and drafts a welcome email for their manager.

scenarios.title: Recurring finance check
scenarios.need: I want our finance agent to wake up on a schedule by itself, find overdue invoices and email the team a short list of what still needs chasing.
scenarios.text: A timer wakes the agent on a schedule to find overdue invoices and email the finance team a short summary of what still needs chasing.

scenarios.title: Policy answers
scenarios.need: I'm building an HR agent and want it to answer leave and expenses questions only from the policy documents we keep on SharePoint.
scenarios.text: An HR agent answers leave and expenses questions from policy documents on SharePoint, so staff get consistent answers without emailing the People team.

scenarios.title: Approved websites only
scenarios.need: I'm building a customer support agent and want it to search only our own help-centre pages, not the whole internet, when it answers.
scenarios.text: A support agent searches only the company's own help-centre pages, so customers get answers from approved public sites rather than the whole web.

scenarios.title: Equipment lookup
scenarios.need: I'm building an agent for our field technicians and want it to answer their questions from the equipment records we keep in Dataverse.
scenarios.text: A field-service agent answers technicians' questions using equipment records stored in Dataverse, so they don't have to call the back office.

scenarios.title: Pilot group trial
scenarios.need: I'm in IT and want a small pilot group to try Microsoft's new preview agents before general release, while everyone else carries on as usual.
scenarios.text: An IT admin switches access on for a small pilot group only, so selected colleagues can test new agents while everyone else carries on as usual.

scenarios.title: Champions go first
scenarios.need: I want our Copilot champions to get early access to Microsoft's experimental agents and report back before we roll them out more widely.
scenarios.text: An adoption lead asks IT to enrol Copilot champions, who try preview agents from the Agent Store and report back on what works before a wider rollout.

scenarios.title: Review before enabling
scenarios.need: I want to understand the preview terms, and what if anything gets switched on automatically, before we sign up for Microsoft's early-access previews.
scenarios.text: A security officer reads the preview terms first and notes that AI providers are never switched on automatically: each model needs separate approval in the admin centre.

scenarios.title: Client meeting prep
scenarios.need: I want AI to gather our recent emails, meetings and files before tomorrow's client call, then write a one-page brief in Word and save it to OneDrive.
scenarios.text: Before a client call, it gathers recent emails, meetings and files, then drafts a one-page Word brief saved to OneDrive.

scenarios.title: Interview scheduling
scenarios.need: I need times found for three candidate interviews and the invitations drafted, but I want to approve every email before anything is sent.
scenarios.text: A recruiter asks it to find slots for three interviews and draft the invitations, then approves the emails before anything is sent.

scenarios.title: Scheduled weekly report
scenarios.need: I want the week's project updates from emails and Teams compiled into a short leadership report every Friday, without asking for it each time.
scenarios.text: Every Friday, Cowork runs a scheduled prompt that compiles the week's project updates from emails and Teams into a short report for the leadership team.

scenarios.title: Channel follow-ups
scenarios.need: I want something that keeps watching our project channel in the background and follows up unanswered questions, so they don't stall while we're busy.
scenarios.text: It keeps an eye on a project channel and follows up on unanswered threads, so questions don't stall while the team is busy.

scenarios.title: Morning inbox sweep
scenarios.need: I want our shared supplier inbox reviewed in the background each morning, with a summary of what needs attention posted to the finance team's channel.
scenarios.text: Each morning it reviews a shared Outlook inbox for new supplier queries and posts a short summary of what needs attention to the finance team's Teams channel.

scenarios.title: Ask it in Teams
scenarios.need: I want to @mention an AI teammate in Teams with requests, knowing it works under its own governed identity and asks me before sensitive actions.
scenarios.text: A sales manager @mentions it in Teams with a request. In preview, it's designed to work under its own governed identity and ask for sign-off on sensitive actions.

scenarios.title: Invoice processing
scenarios.need: I'm building an agent that reads supplier invoices, matches them to purchase orders and routes exceptions for approval, planning its own steps and adapting when one fails.
scenarios.text: An agent reads supplier invoices, matches them to purchase orders and routes any exceptions to an approver, adjusting when a step fails.

scenarios.title: Weekly report pack
scenarios.need: I'm a maker building an agent that gathers sales figures from our connected systems and creates an Excel workbook and a slide deck for Monday's leadership meeting.
scenarios.text: A maker's agent gathers sales figures from connected systems and creates an Excel workbook and a PowerPoint summary ready for Monday's leadership meeting.

scenarios.title: Shared team skills
scenarios.need: Our compliance team wrote a contract-review checklist and wants to package it once so several of our agents follow exactly the same instructions.
scenarios.text: A compliance team packages its contract-review checklist as a skill and adds it to several agents, so each one follows the same instructions.

scenarios.title: Build once, reuse
scenarios.need: I build agents in GitHub Copilot, Foundry and Copilot Studio, and I want them all to share the same company context instead of wiring it up for each.
scenarios.text: A developer reuses the same organisational context across agents built for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Foundry and Copilot Studio, rather than rebuilding it for each.

scenarios.title: Grounded business answers
scenarios.need: I manage our stores and want Copilot's answers about store performance to come straight from our company's own Power BI data models.
scenarios.text: A retail manager asks Copilot about store performance, and the answer can be grounded in the company's own Power BI semantic models through Fabric IQ.

scenarios.title: Shared policy library
scenarios.need: Our compliance team wants one curated policy library that several agents can share, honouring sensitivity labels and each person's access.
scenarios.text: A compliance team shares one curated knowledge base of policies across several agents, honouring sensitivity labels and running queries under each caller's identity.

scenarios.title: Board paper polish
scenarios.need: I'm polishing a confidential board paper in Copilot Chat and want to be sure my prompts and its replies won't be used to train AI models.
scenarios.text: A finance manager asks Copilot Chat to tighten a draft board paper, knowing prompts and replies aren't used to train models.

scenarios.title: Hospital privacy review
scenarios.need: I'm our hospital's privacy officer, and I need to confirm which commitments cover staff prompts in Copilot and warn people where web search queries fall outside them.
scenarios.text: A hospital privacy officer confirms HIPAA support applies to properly configured Copilot use, and warns staff that web search queries fall outside that coverage.

scenarios.title: Vendor risk review
scenarios.need: I need evidence for a vendor risk review of how Microsoft encrypts and isolates our Copilot data, and which commitments like GDPR and ISO/IEC 27018 apply.
scenarios.text: A council's IT security lead gathers evidence for a vendor risk review: encryption, tenant isolation, and named commitments such as GDPR and ISO/IEC 27018.

scenarios.title: Daily to-do round-up
scenarios.need: I want a summary of the team's open to-dos and who owns them to arrive every morning, without me retyping the request each day.
scenarios.text: A project manager sets up a daily summary of open action items, so the team starts each morning knowing who owes what.

scenarios.title: Newsletter input gathering
scenarios.need: I chase colleagues for staff newsletter items every week, and I want a repeating request that gathers their inputs for me.
scenarios.text: A council communications officer sets up a repeating prompt that gathers team inputs for the weekly staff newsletter, instead of chasing everyone by hand.

scenarios.title: Customer-meeting prep
scenarios.need: I want to reuse one fill-in-the-blanks request before each recurring customer meeting, just swapping in the customer's name.
scenarios.text: An account manager reuses one fill-in-the-blank prompt to prepare for each recurring customer meeting, swapping in just the customer's name.

scenarios.title: Demystify a dashboard
scenarios.need: I've got a busy finance dashboard open in our reporting app and want Copilot to look at my screen with me and explain each chart while we talk.
scenarios.text: A finance analyst shares a dense dashboard on screen and asks Copilot to explain what each chart shows and which figures to check first.

scenarios.title: New-starter walk-through
scenarios.need: I'm new and stuck on our expense claim system. I want Copilot to see my screen and talk me through each step, without taking over.
scenarios.text: A new starter shares their screen and asks Copilot to talk them through submitting an expense claim, one step at a time.

scenarios.title: Point your phone camera
scenarios.need: I'm facing an unfamiliar control panel in the plant room and want to point my phone at it and ask Copilot what each label and switch does.
scenarios.text: A facilities technician points a phone camera at an unfamiliar control panel and asks Copilot what each label and switch is for.

scenarios.title: Decode an error message
scenarios.need: I keep getting a confusing error message in an app on my laptop, and I want Copilot to look at it with me and talk me through fixing it.
scenarios.text: An admin officer shares their screen showing a confusing error message and asks Copilot to explain what it means and talk them through the fix, one step at a time.

scenarios.title: Prepare for the day
scenarios.need: I want to talk through today's priorities out loud and have Copilot answer back, suggesting what to tackle first and what to hand off.
scenarios.text: A sales manager talks through the day's priorities and gets Copilot to suggest, out loud, what to tackle first and what to delegate.

scenarios.title: Brainstorm hands free
scenarios.need: I want to brainstorm lesson activities by talking with Copilot while I set up my classroom, then read back over what we said later.
scenarios.text: A teacher brainstorms lesson activities with Copilot out loud while setting up the classroom, then skims the text transcript afterwards.

scenarios.title: Rehearse a pitch
scenarios.need: I want to rehearse my client pitch by saying it out loud, get spoken coaching back, and cut in whenever I want to try a different angle.
scenarios.text: A graduate analyst rehearses a client pitch aloud, gets spoken coaching from Copilot, and interrupts to try a different angle.

scenarios.title: Talk through a decision
scenarios.need: I'm torn between two venues for our team offsite and want to weigh them up by talking with Copilot, then keep a written record of what we covered.
scenarios.text: An office manager talks through two venue options out loud with Copilot, hears its take on the pros and cons, then copies the key points from the text transcript into an email.
