scenarios.title: New hire's starting point
scenarios.need: I'm on my first day and want one place to chat with Copilot, search, find agents and launch Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
scenarios.text: A new hire signs in with their work account and finds chat, search, agents and a launcher for Word, Excel and PowerPoint all in one place.

scenarios.title: Delegate multistep jobs
scenarios.need: I want to hand off a multistep job from the navigation pane of my everyday Copilot starting point, and come back later to review the finished to-dos.
scenarios.text: A project coordinator hands a multistep job to Cowork from the navigation pane, then returns later to review the finished to-dos.

scenarios.title: Work versus personal
scenarios.need: I use Copilot with both a work and a personal account, and want to see which one I'm signed into and know the two stay separate.
scenarios.text: A consultant using both a work and a personal account checks the Work or Personal label beside their profile, knowing the two stay separate.

scenarios.title: Invoice from a PO
scenarios.need: I have a purchase-order PDF and want an invoice document filled in from it, so I only need to check the figures before sending.
scenarios.text: An accounts officer points Copilot at a purchase-order PDF and asks it to fill in an invoice, then checks the figures before sending.

scenarios.title: Update a regulatory package
scenarios.need: I need last year's regulatory submission document updated with this year's source files, and I want to review each change it makes.
scenarios.text: A compliance analyst asks Copilot to update last year's regulatory package using this year's source files, then reviews each change it makes.

scenarios.title: Polish a policy draft
scenarios.need: I've got a dense paragraph in my draft policy document and want it rewritten more clearly, choosing whether to replace it or add the new version below.
scenarios.text: An HR manager selects a dense paragraph in a draft policy and uses Auto Rewrite to make it clearer, choosing whether to replace or insert below.

scenarios.title: First draft from a blank page
scenarios.need: I'm staring at an empty document and need a first draft of a customer brief for our new recycling service, with background, benefits, risks and next steps.
scenarios.text: Describe the document you want, such as a brief with background, benefits, risks and next steps, and Copilot drafts it for you to keep, discard or keep refining.

scenarios.title: Tighten a section for executives
scenarios.need: I need a long section of my project report made more concise and professional for the executive team, without changing what it means.
scenarios.text: Select the section and ask Copilot to make it concise and professional for executives, then choose Replace, Insert below or Regenerate after reviewing it.

scenarios.title: Question a long document
scenarios.need: I'm editing a 25-page service agreement and, before I send it, want to know which parts may confuse the customer and what decisions are still open.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot questions about the open document, such as what may be unclear to a customer or what decisions are needed. In Chat only mode it answers without changing the file.

scenarios.title: Turn text into a table
scenarios.need: I've got a long paragraph in my report listing tasks, owners and due dates, and want it turned into a neat table right there in the report.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot to turn the text into a table with columns such as task, owner, due date and status, then review the result before keeping it.

scenarios.title: Proposal to client deck
scenarios.need: I've got a Word proposal and want it turned into a ten-slide client deck I can edit, instead of starting from blank slides.
scenarios.text: A consultant points Copilot at a Word proposal and asks for a ten-slide client deck, then edits the first draft rather than starting blank.

scenarios.title: Stay on brand
scenarios.need: I want every slide in my new deck to follow our company brand, rather than fixing colours and fonts slide by slide.
scenarios.text: A marketing coordinator selects the company brand so Copilot builds slides that stay on brand, instead of fixing each one by hand.

scenarios.title: Summarise an inherited deck
scenarios.need: I've inherited a 60-slide training deck and want its key messages pulled out before I update the slides for the new group.
scenarios.text: A training lead asks Copilot to summarise an inherited 60-slide deck into its key messages before updating it for the new cohort.

scenarios.title: Chart slide from a spreadsheet
scenarios.need: I want one extra slide in my quarterly review deck with a chart from the sales spreadsheet in my files and three takeaways underneath.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot to add a slide with a chart based on the spreadsheet you reference and to summarise the top takeaways under it, right inside your open presentation.

scenarios.title: Image for a title slide
scenarios.need: I want a custom image of a busy coffee shop generated and placed straight onto the title slide I'm working on.
scenarios.text: Request an image in Copilot Chat in PowerPoint and it can generate one and insert it directly onto your slide, or return it in chat for you to place yourself.

scenarios.title: Get ready for tough questions
scenarios.need: I'm presenting my slides to the board on Thursday and want to know where the story is weak and which questions they're likely to ask.
scenarios.text: The Prepare for Questions skill analyses your presentation to find weak points and anticipate audience questions, so you can tighten the story before you present.

scenarios.title: Restyle a messy slide
scenarios.need: I've got one messy slide in my deck and want it restyled to match the others, with a cleaner layout and clearer visual hierarchy.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot to restyle the slide to match the rest of the deck. It can improve the layout and visual hierarchy and, with a Brand Kit, use your branded images.

scenarios.title: Outline before slides
scenarios.need: I want to see, reorder and trim the proposed list of topics for my client pitch deck before any slides are drafted.
scenarios.text: A sales director typed a prompt for a client pitch, then reordered and trimmed the proposed topics before Copilot drafted any slides.

scenarios.title: Refine the storyline
scenarios.need: I want to keep refining the list of topics for my deck until the storyline feels right, and only then have the first slides drafted.
scenarios.text: A programme manager refined the topic outline until the storyline felt right, then let Copilot draft the first version of the deck.

scenarios.title: On-brand first draft
scenarios.need: I've agreed the outline of topics, and now I want the first draft of the deck to use our branded template instead of a generic theme.
scenarios.text: A communications lead used the companion Brand manager so the first draft followed the company's branded template, rather than a generic theme.

scenarios.title: Tidy a messy export
scenarios.need: I've got a messy ledger export in my spreadsheet and want it cleaned up with a variance column added, then to check what changed.
scenarios.text: A finance analyst asks Copilot to tidy a messy ledger export and add a variance column, then reviews the changes it made.

scenarios.title: PivotTable on request
scenarios.need: I want a summary table and chart of revenue by region and quarter built from the sales data in my workbook, linked back to the source.
scenarios.text: A sales manager asks for a PivotTable and chart of revenue by region and quarter, and Copilot builds both with links back to the source data.

scenarios.title: Plan before it edits
scenarios.need: I want to read and approve the proposed steps before anything changes in my headcount workbook.
scenarios.text: An HR analyst uses plan mode on a headcount workbook, reads Copilot's proposed steps and approves them before anything in the file changes.

scenarios.title: Chart from a table
scenarios.need: I want a line chart of monthly visitor numbers from the table in my open workbook, placed beside the data so I can tweak it.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot to chart the table and it creates an editable chart in your workbook, linked to the source data, which you can adjust like any other chart.

scenarios.title: Add a calculated column
scenarios.need: I need a new column in my staff training spreadsheet that works out how many days are left until each person's certificate expires.
scenarios.text: Copilot can add a formula column that calculates the days remaining for every row, so the workings stay in the sheet for you to check and edit.

scenarios.title: Colour-code late orders
scenarios.need: I want every order in my delivery tracker spreadsheet that's more than a week late to turn red automatically, so the team spots them at a glance.
scenarios.text: Copilot can apply conditional formatting so late orders are highlighted automatically, and the rule stays in the workbook for you to adjust later.

scenarios.title: Spot unusual figures
scenarios.need: I want to know which of our 40 stores' weekly sales figures look unusual compared with the rest, in the workbook I have open.
scenarios.text: Ask Copilot questions about your data and it shows insights such as trends and outliers as charts, PivotTables or summaries. Chat only mode leaves the workbook unchanged.

scenarios.title: Dashboard-style summary sheet
scenarios.need: I want a one-sheet overview added to our annual budget workbook, with a few charts and a summary table my manager can read at a glance.
scenarios.text: Copilot can build a dashboard-style sheet with charts and a PivotTable linked to your data, and everything it creates stays editable.

scenarios.title: Variance workbook
scenarios.need: I want raw ledger data turned into a table, a summary table and a budget-versus-actual chart in one go, then a rundown of what changed.
scenarios.text: A finance analyst asks Copilot to turn raw ledger data into a table, PivotTable and chart of budget versus actual, then reviews what changed.

scenarios.title: Policy refresh
scenarios.need: I want last year's leave policy restructured into plain-English sections right inside the open file, then a summary of what changed.
scenarios.text: An HR advisor opens last year's leave policy in Word and asks Copilot to restructure it into plain-English sections, then reads the summary of changes.

scenarios.title: Pitch deck from chat
scenarios.need: I want a customer pitch deck built straight from a Copilot chat and saved as a file, after it asks me a few questions.
scenarios.text: A sales lead asks the PowerPoint Agent in chat for a customer pitch deck; it asks clarifying questions, builds the file and saves it to OneDrive.

scenarios.title: Champion kickoff briefing
scenarios.need: I want to explain to new staff where Pages and agents came from, starting with Microsoft's September 2024 Copilot announcements.
scenarios.text: A Copilot champion revisits the September 2024 announcements to explain to new staff where Pages and agents came from, in plain English.

scenarios.title: Release-history review
scenarios.need: I'm building a timeline of what shipped when and need to separate what went generally available in September 2024 from previews announced alongside it.
scenarios.text: An IT lead builds a timeline of what shipped when, separating generally available items from previews announced alongside, such as Python in Excel and Prioritize my inbox.

scenarios.title: Learning path refresh
scenarios.need: I want practice exercises built from the Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook upgrades Microsoft announced for Copilot on 16 September 2024.
scenarios.text: A trainer turns the announcement's Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook upgrades into short practice exercises and adds them to the team's Copilot learning path.

scenarios.title: Champion explainer session
scenarios.need: Staff keep mixing up Microsoft's April 2025 Copilot announcements with the 2024 ones, and I want to explain what Search, Create and Notebooks arrived with.
scenarios.text: A Copilot champion explains what the April 2025 announcement promised: Search, Create, Notebooks and the Agent Store, so staff stop confusing it with the 2024 one.

scenarios.title: Trace the rollout path
scenarios.need: I want to trace how Researcher and Analyst moved from early preview to general availability, starting from Microsoft's April 2025 Copilot announcements that featured them.
scenarios.text: An IT lead reviews the April 2025 announcement to trace how Researcher and Analyst moved from the Frontier program to general availability for licensed users.

scenarios.title: Curriculum update
scenarios.need: I'm rebuilding our Copilot training around the app's Search, Create, Notebooks and agents areas, plus memory, as Microsoft announced them in April 2025.
scenarios.text: A trainer rebuilds the Copilot curriculum around the app's four areas, Search, Create, Notebooks and agents, and adds a module on memory and personalisation.

scenarios.title: Rollout plan refresh
scenarios.need: I'm updating our rollout plan around Microsoft's March 2026 announcements, such as Cowork, agents in chat and in-app agentic editing, and choosing pilot teams.
scenarios.text: A Copilot champion rebuilds the rollout plan around Cowork, agents in chat and in-app agentic editing, deciding which teams to pilot first.

scenarios.title: Release notes review
scenarios.need: I want to work out what Microsoft's March 2026 Copilot announcements need from IT, from Frontier access to Agent 365 and licensing.
scenarios.text: An IT lead reads the March 2026 announcement and later release notes to see what needs admin attention, from Frontier access to Agent 365 and licensing.

scenarios.title: Training plan update
scenarios.need: I want our curriculum to cover what Microsoft announced in March 2026: Cowork, chat-first file creation and agent help inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
scenarios.text: A learning and development trainer updates the Copilot curriculum so staff learn Cowork, chat-first file creation and agent-assisted Word, Excel and PowerPoint, not just prompting basics.

scenarios.title: Workshop day
scenarios.need: I'm in back-to-back client workshops all day and want my incoming Teams calls answered, each caller's reason noted and callbacks booked.
scenarios.text: A consultant running back-to-back client workshops lets it screen external calls, collect each caller's reason and book callbacks, then reads the summaries in Call history afterwards.

scenarios.title: Out-of-office cover
scenarios.need: I'm going on leave and want my external Teams calls taken for me, with each caller's reason noted and callbacks booked for when I'm back.
scenarios.text: A finance manager on leave lets it take external calls, noting each reason and booking callbacks for after she returns.

scenarios.title: Step in when urgent
scenarios.need: I want to see a live preview of the caller's reason while AI screens an incoming call for me, and pick up myself if it sounds urgent.
scenarios.text: An operations manager sees the screening banner, watches a live preview of the caller's reason, and picks up from Call history when it sounds urgent.

scenarios.title: Jump to your mentions
scenarios.need: I was mentioned in a two-hour pipeline review I couldn't attend, and I want to jump straight to those moments and see AI-suggested tasks.
scenarios.text: A sales manager, mentioned twice in a long pipeline review, jumps to those timeline markers and reads the AI-recommended tasks before replying to the team.

scenarios.title: Follow up a call
scenarios.need: I've just had a Teams call with a resident and want notes and suggested tasks generated from it automatically, so I can check them against what I promised.
scenarios.text: After a Teams call with a resident, a council officer opens the call recap for AI notes and recommended tasks, then checks them against what was promised.

scenarios.title: Watch the highlights
scenarios.need: I missed a recorded onboarding session and want a short narrated highlights video first, before deciding which parts of the full recording to watch.
scenarios.text: A training coordinator who missed a recorded onboarding session watches its narrated video highlights first, then decides which parts of the full recording are worth the time.

scenarios.title: Listen on the drive in
scenarios.need: I missed three transcribed project meetings yesterday and want one podcast-style summary of them all that I can listen to on my drive in.
scenarios.text: A site manager selects yesterday's three transcribed meetings and generates an audio recap: one podcast-like summary of key discussions and decisions to play on the go.

scenarios.title: Choosing laptops for a team
scenarios.need: I'm buying new laptops for my team and need to be sure they have the hardware to run Windows AI features on the device itself.
scenarios.text: An IT buyer confirms new laptops meet the Copilot+ PC bar (a 40+ TOPS NPU) before promising staff on-device AI features like Click to Do.

scenarios.title: Testing on-device AI
scenarios.need: I'm a developer and need a laptop with a powerful built-in AI chip, so I can run and test an AI model locally while watching how hard the chip works.
scenarios.text: A developer tests an on-device AI feature on a Copilot+ PC, using Task Manager to watch NPU usage and Windows ML to run the model there.

scenarios.title: Pilot with teachers
scenarios.need: Our school is weighing up a laptop refresh and wants to trial a few machines built for on-device AI with teachers before deciding.
scenarios.text: A school IT lead pilots a handful of Copilot+ PCs with teachers before deciding whether to refresh the wider laptop fleet.

scenarios.title: Quick question mid-task
scenarios.need: I'm halfway through a task and want a single press on my keyboard to bring up Copilot for a quick question, without hunting for an icon.
scenarios.text: A project manager presses the key mid-task, types a quick question into Copilot and gets an answer without opening a browser tab.

scenarios.title: Voice chat while typing
scenarios.need: I want to press and hold something on my keyboard to start a spoken chat with Copilot while I keep typing up a support ticket.
scenarios.text: A support engineer holds the key to start a voice chat and talks through a troubleshooting checklist while still typing up the ticket.

scenarios.title: Managed laptop setup
scenarios.need: I'm an IT admin and want to set, by policy, which app opens from the dedicated launcher on our new managed laptop keyboards.
scenarios.text: An IT admin uses the SetCopilotHardwareKey policy to choose which app the key launches on managed laptops.

scenarios.title: Message from the screen
scenarios.need: I can see a candidate's email address in a PDF on my screen and want to start a message to them straight from it, without copying it anywhere.
scenarios.text: A recruiter spots a candidate's email address inside a PDF and starts a message from it, without copying it into another app first.

scenarios.title: Quick on-device summary
scenarios.need: I've got a long passage of an article on screen and want a quick summary of just that bit, worked out on my own laptop, before my meeting.
scenarios.text: A policy analyst selects a long passage in a web article and asks for a quick on-device summary before heading into a meeting.

scenarios.title: Quick photo clean-up
scenarios.need: I've spotted a product photo on my screen and want to strip out its background quickly so I can reuse it, without saving and opening it first.
scenarios.text: A marketing coordinator spots a product image on screen and sends it to Paint to remove its background before reusing it.

scenarios.title: Make it more formal
scenarios.need: I've typed a chatty update in an app with no writing help, and I want to select it on my screen and get a more formal version in seconds.
scenarios.text: A team leader selects a casual draft on screen and chooses Rewrite (Formal), which runs on the device, to get a more formal version without switching apps first.

scenarios.title: Find the lost chart
scenarios.need: I saw a chart last week in a presentation but can't remember the file. I want to describe it and jump back to the moment I saw it.
scenarios.text: An analyst remembers a chart in a presentation but not the file name, describes it in the search box and jumps back to that moment.

scenarios.title: IT policy decision
scenarios.need: I'm an IT lead deciding whether to allow the feature that keeps searchable snapshots of people's screens on our managed laptops.
scenarios.text: An IT lead reads the Manage Recall guidance before deciding whether to allow it, since it's removed by default on managed commercial devices.

scenarios.title: Pause for sensitive work
scenarios.need: I'm about to review confidential client files and want my laptop to stop saving snapshots of my screen until tomorrow.
scenarios.text: A consultant chooses Pause until tomorrow before reviewing confidential client files; snapshots resume automatically at midnight.

scenarios.title: Work and personal accounts
scenarios.need: I use Copilot on my laptop for both work and personal things, and I want to switch accounts while keeping the two sets of chats separate.
scenarios.text: A consultant uses the account switcher to move between a work account and a personal one, knowing the two sets of chats and data stay separate.

scenarios.title: Find a file quickly
scenarios.need: I want to ask Copilot on my laptop to find a budget spreadsheet saved on the device, without clicking through folders.
scenarios.text: An office manager asks the app to find a budget spreadsheet saved on the laptop, without browsing folders.

scenarios.title: Help with Windows settings
scenarios.need: I'm finding the text on my laptop screen hard to read, and I want to ask Copilot which display setting fixes it and be taken straight there.
scenarios.text: A call-centre agent types 'Make my screen easier to read' and Copilot guides them to the relevant Windows setting.

scenarios.title: Hands-free calendar summary
scenarios.need: I'm making coffee near my desk and want to get Copilot on my PC listening just by saying a phrase, then hear today's calendar summarised.
scenarios.text: A busy manager says the phrase while making coffee and asks for a summary of today's calendar.

scenarios.title: Brainstorm out loud
scenarios.need: I'm tidying my desk and want to start a chat with Copilot on my PC just by speaking, without touching the mouse or keyboard, to brainstorm ideas.
scenarios.text: A teacher preparing a lesson says the phrase and brainstorms activity ideas out loud while tidying their desk.

scenarios.title: Quick translation
scenarios.need: I've got a guest at my front desk and want to get Copilot on my PC going just by speaking, then have it translate a short message, hands free.
scenarios.text: A front-desk receptionist says the phrase and asks Copilot to translate a short message for an international guest, hands free.

scenarios.title: Weighing roadmap options
scenarios.need: I want two roadmap options weighed carefully, with the pros, cons and hidden risks, and to follow the reasoning as it works.
scenarios.text: A product manager asks for the pros, cons and hidden risks of two roadmap options, and follows the reasoning as it unfolds.

scenarios.title: Untangling a formula
scenarios.need: I've pasted a stubborn nested formula into a chat because my totals don't match, and I want careful step-by-step problem-solving to find why.
scenarios.text: A finance analyst pastes a stubborn nested formula and asks for careful step-by-step problem-solving to find why the totals don't match.

scenarios.title: Exploring both perspectives
scenarios.need: I want a careful, nuanced comparison of two perspectives on a historical event for my class, which I'll then turn into discussion questions.
scenarios.text: A history teacher asks for a nuanced comparison of two perspectives on an event, then turns it into discussion questions.

scenarios.title: Assign a Copilot licence
scenarios.need: I'd like to just type a request to give our new lecturer a Copilot licence before she starts on Monday, then review the change before it's made.
scenarios.text: A university IT officer asks the agent to assign a Copilot licence to a new lecturer, reviews the proposed change and confirms it.

scenarios.title: Review and block agents
scenarios.need: I'd like to ask in plain language which agents we have, check how much each is used and block one, without clicking through admin pages.
scenarios.text: A bank's technology risk lead asks for agents in the registry, checks their usage analytics and blocks one that shouldn't be there.

scenarios.title: Triage Teams call quality
scenarios.need: Our contact-centre team says their calls keep sounding choppy. I want to ask in plain words for an analysis of their call and meeting quality.
scenarios.text: A contact-centre IT analyst asks the agent to analyse call and meeting quality for a team reporting choppy audio, then decides what to escalate.

scenarios.title: Sensitive policy update
scenarios.need: I'm about to email staff about a policy change and want my draft checked so it reads as supportive rather than blunt.
scenarios.text: An HR advisor drafts a policy-change email and asks Copilot to review the tone, so it reads supportive rather than blunt before it goes to staff.

scenarios.title: Calming an upset client
scenarios.need: I've written an email reply to an upset client and want suggestions on tone and clarity that I can apply all at once.
scenarios.text: A customer-service lead replying to an upset client reviews the draft's tone and clarity, applies all suggestions, then rereads the result before sending.

scenarios.title: Fresh feedback on mobile
scenarios.need: I've drafted an email reply to parents on my phone and want fresh feedback on how it might land before I send it.
scenarios.text: A school principal drafts a reply to parents on their phone, taps Regenerate for fresh feedback, then edits the wording by hand before sending.

scenarios.title: Escalations stand out
scenarios.need: I want new emails mentioning 'outage' or from key account owners to stand out as soon as they arrive on busy mornings.
scenarios.text: A customer-support manager tells Copilot that mentions of 'outage' and messages from key account owners are important, so urgent escalations stand out on busy mornings.

scenarios.title: Spot staffing requests
scenarios.need: I want incoming mail from our clinical director, or mentioning rostering, to be marked as important among all the routine notices.
scenarios.text: A hospital operations lead adds the clinical director and the keyword 'rostering' to their instructions, so staffing requests get an up arrow among routine notices.

scenarios.title: Month-end focus
scenarios.need: I want new mail about the month-end close or from the CFO marked as important, with a note explaining why each one was marked.
scenarios.text: A finance analyst names 'month-end close' as a topic and the CFO as a person, then checks the reading pane to see why a message was marked.

scenarios.title: Back from leave
scenarios.need: I'm back from a week away and want the key points of a long reply-all email thread shown at the top, with links to check who approved what.
scenarios.text: After a week away, a project manager reads the key points of a long thread first, then jumps to the cited emails to check who approved what.

scenarios.title: Digest a supplier PDF
scenarios.need: I've been emailed a 40-page PDF by a supplier, and I want the gist straight from the message before deciding whether to read it all.
scenarios.text: A procurement officer selects Summarize a file on a supplier's PDF attachment in new Outlook to get the gist before deciding whether to read all of it.

scenarios.title: Catch up on mobile
scenarios.need: I want the gist of a long client email thread on my phone between visits, without scrolling through every reply.
scenarios.text: Between visits, a field sales rep taps the Copilot icon on their phone's toolbar and reads a long client thread's summary under the email.

scenarios.title: Labelling client files
scenarios.need: We want client files encrypted so Copilot only returns their content to people who hold rights to both view and extract it.
scenarios.text: A law firm applies encrypting sensitivity labels to client files, so Copilot only returns that content to people holding both the VIEW and EXTRACT usage rights.

scenarios.title: Stopping card-number pastes
scenarios.need: I want to warn or block staff who paste credit card numbers into ChatGPT on their work Windows PCs.
scenarios.text: A retailer's security team uses Endpoint DLP on onboarded Windows PCs to warn or block staff pasting credit card numbers into ChatGPT.

scenarios.title: Finding AI interactions
scenarios.need: I need staff's Copilot prompts and answers to be searchable in legal investigations and kept for the same period as our other records.
scenarios.text: A public-sector compliance officer searches eDiscovery for 'Copilot activity' and sets retention policies, so AI interactions are found and kept like other records.

scenarios.title: Keeping labelled files out of answers
scenarios.need: I want Copilot to stop using any file or email we've marked Highly Confidential when it writes answers, even for staff who are allowed to open them.
scenarios.text: A defence supplier's compliance team creates a data loss prevention policy for the Copilot location, so files and emails with the Highly Confidential sensitivity label aren't used when Copilot generates responses.

scenarios.title: Client matter lock-down
scenarios.need: I want a client-matter site opened only by the matter team's security group, so other partners can't get in, even with an old link.
scenarios.text: A law firm limits a client-matter site to the matter team's security group, so partners elsewhere can't open it, even with an old link.

scenarios.title: Dynamic project team
scenarios.need: I want only current members of our research project to open its SharePoint site, so people who change departments lose access without anyone editing permissions.
scenarios.text: A hospital research site is limited to a dynamic security group of current project staff, so people who move departments lose access without anyone editing permissions.

scenarios.title: Deal team confidentiality
scenarios.need: Our deal team's site must be limited to one Microsoft 365 group, so colleagues with stray permissions can't open it or see its files in Copilot.
scenarios.text: A bank limits its deal-team site to one Microsoft 365 group, so colleagues with stray permissions can't open it or see its files in Copilot.

scenarios.title: Pause Finance and HR sites
scenarios.need: I want Copilot and organisation-wide search to skip our Finance and HR sites before rollout while owners review permissions, without anyone losing access.
scenarios.text: Before a Copilot rollout, an IT admin restricts the Finance and HR sites so Copilot and organisation-wide search skip them while owners review permissions.

scenarios.title: Phased Copilot rollout
scenarios.need: We're turning Copilot on in phases and want sites we haven't checked yet kept out of Copilot answers, one site at a time, until we get to them.
scenarios.text: A university IT team rolls Copilot out in phases, restricting sites it hasn't reviewed yet so staff don't see their files surface in Copilot answers.

scenarios.title: Delegated site admin
scenarios.need: I've been given control by IT to keep my department's site out of Copilot answers myself, and I expect to give a reason whenever I change it.
scenarios.text: Once IT delegates the setting, a council department's site admin restricts their own site and must give a justification when they change it.

scenarios.title: Stopgap during permission audit
scenarios.need: I needed Copilot and organisation-wide search to draw mainly on a short list of up to 100 vetted sites last year, while we audited permissions.
scenarios.text: A manufacturer's admin allow-listed its reviewed sites, so Copilot and organisation-wide search mostly drew on vetted sites while the remaining permissions were audited.

scenarios.title: Planning the replacement
scenarios.need: Our tenant still limits Copilot to a list of up to 100 approved sites, and I need to plan our move off that soon-to-retire tenant setting.
scenarios.text: An IT lead whose tenant already uses the allow list plans a switch to site-level Restricted Content Discovery for the sites that need hiding.

scenarios.title: Briefing leadership on limits
scenarios.need: Our leadership asks why sites shared in Teams or Outlook, or recently opened, still showed up in Copilot after we limited it to 100 approved sites.
scenarios.text: A consultant explains to a council's leadership why recently accessed sites, and sites shared in Teams or Outlook, could still appear despite the allow list.

scenarios.title: Find HR quick wins
scenarios.need: I lead HR and want to browse AI ideas organised for my function, then download a guide to help pick two quick wins.
scenarios.text: An HR lead opens the Human Resources function, browses the AI scenarios and downloads a scenario guide to pick two quick wins for their team.

scenarios.title: Brief the board
scenarios.need: I want a day-in-the-life guide showing what practical AI help looks like at a nonprofit, to show our board.
scenarios.text: A nonprofit's fundraising manager browses Nonprofit scenarios and picks a day-in-the-life guide to show the board what practical AI help looks like.

scenarios.title: Plan a team workshop
scenarios.need: I'm running a workshop on agents for our finance team and want a downloadable kit of real AI scenarios for that function.
scenarios.text: An adoption champion filters to Agents scenarios, then downloads a functional scenario kit to run a workshop for the finance team.

scenarios.title: Same idea, different words
scenarios.need: I asked Copilot for our USA launch plans and want to know what lets it also find files I can open that say 'United States' or 'U.S.A' instead.
scenarios.text: A marketing manager asks Copilot for USA launch plans and also gets documents saying 'United States' or 'U.S.A', provided she can open them.

scenarios.title: Keep a site out
scenarios.need: I've set a confidential site to not appear in search results and want to know if that also drops it from the index Copilot uses to match ideas by meaning.
scenarios.text: An IT admin sets a confidential SharePoint site to not appear in search results, which also removes it from the semantic index.

scenarios.title: Searching a contracts library
scenarios.need: I want Copilot to use our contracts library's column details, like client and expiry date, as extra clues when it looks for the right contract by meaning.
scenarios.text: A paralegal attaches a SharePoint contracts library in Copilot on the web; its column metadata gives Copilot extra signals for finding the right documents.

scenarios.title: Copilot rollout prep
scenarios.need: I want one SharePoint admin toolkit to tackle oversharing and clear out stale sites before we switch Copilot on for thousands of staff.
scenarios.text: A state government IT team works through the oversharing tools and tidies stale sites before switching Copilot on for thousands of staff.

scenarios.title: Tackle abandoned sites
scenarios.need: Our old course and project sites are gathering dust, and I want a SharePoint admin policy that finds inactive ones so staff and Copilot stop wading through them.
scenarios.text: A university IT team applies an inactive sites policy to abandoned course and project sites so staff and Copilot aren't wading through stale content.

scenarios.title: Spot and fix oversharing
scenarios.need: I want the full SharePoint governance toolkit, so I can spot a clinic site shared with all staff in a report and then get its owners to review access.
scenarios.text: A healthcare IT lead spots a clinic site shared with all internal users in a governance report, then sends its owners a site access review.

scenarios.title: Anyone links clean-up
scenarios.need: I want to send a campaign site's owner a built-in, tailored request from an admin report, asking them to tidy up its many 'Anyone' links themselves.
scenarios.text: A retail IT admin spots a campaign site with many Anyone links and emails its owner a tailored request to tidy up sharing.

scenarios.title: Tighten internal-wide sharing
scenarios.need: I've picked staff sites shared with 'Everyone except external users' and want each site's owner asked to check who really needs access.
scenarios.text: A school's IT coordinator picks staff sites shared with 'Everyone except external users' and asks each owner to check who really needs access.

scenarios.title: Customised owner guidance
scenarios.need: I want client-site owners from our oversharing baseline report sent a customised request, linking to our sharing guidance page, to check and fix access.
scenarios.text: A consulting firm's admin starts from the oversharing baseline report and sends client-site owners a customised message linking to a SharePoint page of sharing guidance.

scenarios.title: Back from leave
scenarios.need: I'm back from leave and want last week's meeting recording, notes and shared files in one spot, rather than asking someone for a rundown.
scenarios.text: A project manager back from leave opens last week's recap to watch the recording, skim the notes and open shared files, rather than asking for a rundown.

scenarios.title: Town hall catch-up
scenarios.need: I missed the live town hall and want to watch its recording and read the transcript to find the roster announcement.
scenarios.text: A retail store manager who missed the live town hall opens its recap later, watching the recording and reading the transcript for the roster announcement.

scenarios.title: Email the summary
scenarios.need: I ran a customer workshop in Teams and want to send everyone its AI summary by email, editing the drafted Outlook message before it goes.
scenarios.text: After a customer workshop, a sales lead shares the AI summary to email from the recap, edits the drafted Outlook message and sends it to the team.

scenarios.title: Earlier session in a series
scenarios.need: Our steering committee meets weekly, and I want the agenda, notes and files from the session three weeks ago without digging through my inbox.
scenarios.text: A program coordinator opens the recurring meeting's Recap, picks an earlier occurrence from the dropdown and finds that session's agenda, notes and shared files.

scenarios.title: Clinic bookings
scenarios.need: Our clinic's main phone line needs to answer opening-hours questions in natural conversation, book appointments and put people through to the front desk.
scenarios.text: A clinic lets the agent answer opening-hours questions, book appointments through Microsoft Bookings and route anyone who needs a person to the front desk.

scenarios.title: Order status calls
scenarios.need: Our support line's callers mostly ask about orders, and I want them talking naturally to AI that hands order checks to a Copilot Studio agent.
scenarios.text: A retailer's support line hands callers asking about their orders to a Copilot Studio agent that checks order status, leaving staff free for trickier requests.

scenarios.title: Council enquiries
scenarios.need: Our customer-service line gets endless bin-collection questions. I want callers answered by voice from approved web pages, with complex calls routed to the right queue.
scenarios.text: A council's customer-service line lets the agent answer rates and bin-collection questions from approved web pages and route complex queries to the right call queue.

scenarios.title: Weekly sales meeting
scenarios.need: Our sales team meets around one meeting-room device, and once people opt in, I want the transcript to name who in the room said what.
scenarios.text: After staff opt in under Recognition, a weekly sales meeting's transcript can name who spoke in the room, so follow-ups trace back to who said what.

scenarios.title: Admin rollout checklist
scenarios.need: I manage our meeting-room devices and need to license the room accounts and control voice and face enrolment through policy.
scenarios.text: An IT admin assigns a Teams Rooms Pro licence to the room's resource account and manages voice and face enrolment with the CsTeamsAIPolicy PowerShell policy.

scenarios.title: Answering profile privacy questions
scenarios.need: Staff are asking whether the voice and face profiles that identify them in our meeting rooms train AI models, and when they're deleted.
scenarios.text: A council privacy officer notes Microsoft says voice and face profiles aren't used to train models and are removed on unenrol, or after a year unused.
